To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose and evaluate a novel integer mixed-precision representation of neural network parameters, which is used to train state-of-the- art CNNs on ImageNet-1k, and achieve SOTA accuracy using integer operations.

we present the first mixed precision integer training of state-of-the-art CNNs on ImageNet-1k, using a shared exponent representation and a dynamic fixed point scheme for common neural network operators, and we achieve the highest reported accuracy using integer operations.

(1) we propose a novel shared exponent representation of floating-point tensors, (2) we propose a DFP scheme that allows efficient use of the shared exponent representation for common neural network operators, (3) we develop a convolution kernel for INT16 training, (4) we demonstrate INT16 training of ResNet-50 and GoogLeNet, and (5) we achieve SOTA accuracy for INT16 training of AlexNet, VGG-19, ResNet-101 and ResNet
In summary, our research is concerned with
training deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) on the ImageNet dataset using low precision Integer operations on general purpose (GP) hardware (CPUs/GPUs) to achieve high accuracy and throughput.
training CNNs using low precision Integer arithmetic on General Purpose (GPU) hardware.
the problem of training convolutional neural networks (CNNs) on GPUs using integer operations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the paper presents a new approach to train CNNs using integer arithmetic and shows that the approach can be competitive in terms of accuracy with state of the art FP16 training approaches.
we are the first to report INT16 training results for state-of-the-art neural networks on ImageNet-1k using General-Purpose hardware.
we are the first to report INT16 training on ImageNet-1k with SOTA networks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have achieved SOTA results for mixed precision training on ImageNet-1k dataset using integer operations, and have also shown that the same results can be reproduced on the latest NVIDIA GPUs.
we have achieved state-of-the-art accuracy in mixed precision training of convolutional neural networks using integer operations.
it is the first work to demonstrate the feasibility of training state of the art networks with integer operations on general purpose hardware.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Integer training can achieve the same or better performance than mixed precision floating point training.
integer training can achieve SOTA accuracy on ImageNet-1k dataset with a 1X speedup over FP32 training, and a 1.5X to 2X speedup over mixed precision training.
Integer operations are a viable option for low precision training of neural networks.
